title: When a challenger introduces friction into an institution's own procedures, the institution can only respond by absorbing the cost or denouncing its own framework's legitimacy
body:
- Direct attempts to dismantle an institution force the challenger into a resistance fight and a legitimacy battle, because defenders can recast the challenger as the aggressor.
- Introducing friction inside the institution's existing processes sidesteps that battle by routing pressure through channels the institution itself maintains.
- The institution can then only absorb the friction's cost or denounce the framework on which it has staked its own legitimacy.
conversion: Friction inserted inside an institution's own procedures converts its rules into leverage against it, forcing the institution to absorb the cost or denounce its own framework.
